id_and_class.summary: Jorge Ferrer treats phenomenal consciousness as an embodied, relational event enacted through co-creative engagement between humans and the ‘mystery of the Real’, the creative power of the cosmos. He declines to declare either matter or consciousness the foundation, arguing that current evidence leaves the question open and that reality may be plural and still unfolding.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Co-Creative Participation in the Real

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a participatory event: an activity the cosmos performs and that humans, as the cosmos become self-conscious, continue to co-create through relational engagement.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Left open. Mind and matter may both be foundational, or may both manifest from one or more largely unperceived dimensions of the Real, which Ferrer distinguishes from dual-aspect monism’s single underlying reality.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Undecided by design; Ferrer holds that whether consciousness is foundational or emergent matters less than the quality of engagement through which it appears
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjective experience is tied to a relational field between persons, between body and environment, and between the human and the Real. It is never an isolated ‘inner light’.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Ferrer argues that understanding qualia requires combining first-person (contemplative), second-person (relational), and third-person (laboratory) approaches.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A creative, evolving cosmos (the mystery of the Real); human participants with many ways of knowing (cognitive, emotional, imaginal); enacted spiritual realities that are real but open to re-enactment.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through embodied and relational engagement as well as introspection and experiment. Ferrer calls this epistemology constructivist about knowing and realist about what is known.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A cosmos that complexifies and turns inward, from particles to galaxies, life, mind, culture, and contemplation, with humans as self-conscious participants in that process.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Spiritual and transpersonal experience, Relational and intersubjective experience
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Participatory enaction. Extending Varela, Thompson, and Rosch’s enactive cognition from perception to spiritual life, Ferrer holds that humans bring forth spiritual phenomena and realities through co-creative interplay with the generative force of the cosmos.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Realities, once enacted historically, become more accessible and in a sense ‘given’, yet remain open to re-enactment, as with changing versions of Buddhist emptiness or the Christian God over history.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is located in relations: between persons, between body and world, and between the human and the cosmos.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Human participation is co-creative, shaping which realities become available, so asking about consciousness is itself a participatory act.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: The cosmos shows creative diversification, growing more complex and more inward from matter through life and mind to culture and contemplation; consciousness belongs to that unfolding.
core_claims_and_evidence: Materialism fails to close the explanatory gap of qualia, while foundational idealism commits ‘ontological closure’ by declaring the mystery solved without enough evidence.

Data such as veridical perception in near-death experiences are ‘ontologically polysemic’: even proven survival would not show that consciousness is the foundation of the cosmos, since rich emergentist views could also explain it.
Spiritual realities are enacted through human participation and, once enacted, stay open to creative transformation.
A full account of consciousness needs first-, second-, and third-person methods together.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and phenomenological, drawing on transpersonal psychology and comparative religion

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Ferrer points to near-death veridical perception studies (Van Lommel and colleagues) and neuroimaging of reduced default-mode-network activity in psychedelic states as legitimate data, while holding that they underdetermine the metaphysics.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: By design the theory does not decide between continuity, self-awakening, and an underlying third dimension of the Real, which Ferrer calls the three ‘marvels’. It names consciousness a participatory event that ‘somehow’ manifests, leaving the mechanism open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Ferrer pairs open naturalism, which accepts as real whatever is needed to make sense of the full range of human experience, with metaphysical openness. The result is consistent but deliberately non-committal about foundations.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Ferrer’s plural, multidimensional ontology leaves room for a diversity of post-mortem scenarios without asserting any one.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Humans are co-creative partners in the cosmos’s unfolding, and inquiry into consciousness may be the universe’s own longing to understand itself.
